correctness.rationale: Checked precise Alexander-dual face predicate: 0/1-simplices complete; triangles correspond exactly to connected graph triples (induced 2-paths); tetrahedra to induced squares; no 5-vertex dual faces by triangle-free Mantel bound. For n≥5 the antipodal quotient of Q_n has unique common-neighbor square completions, so each square tetrahedron collapses along a unique triangle and then a free diagonal edge, leaving the square-filled graph plus b far-distance edges. Its square-filled subcomplex is the 2-skeleton of the cubical CW quotient of the n-cube boundary by the free antipodal map, homeomorphic to RP^(n-1). Consequently H1=Z/2, H2=Z^h where h=2^(n-4)(n^2−5n+8)−1, and adding b far edges gives H1=Z^b⊕Z/2. Integral UCT places the Z/2 Ext class in H², while duality shifts it to H~_{N−5}(Δ3), alongside free H~_{N−4}=Z^b. Independently checked n=5 N16 q40,b0,h15, and n=6 N32 q120,b160,h55. Infinite n follows from the covering-space and collapse argument, not these finite samples.
residual_risks: Finite n=5,6 cases cannot prove every dimension; quotient geometry and free-face uniqueness provide the universal argument.
The n=4 exception precludes unqualified extension below n=5.

value.rationale: A uniform infinite family of highly symmetric folded cubical graphs has integral next-to-top torsion and complete explicit free ranks, yielding nonshellability at every n≥5. The proof explains the exact Z/2 obstruction through a projective-space 2-skeleton and integral UCT rather than ad hoc finite computations. This structurally motivated classification is not a routine special case of the edge-disjoint-squares theorem.
residual_risks: All-n group structure strongly motivates the theorem; new geometric consequences beyond torsion nonshellability not asserted.

limitations: No homotopy type or equivariant module for the original ordinary 3-cut complex.
